exposure: higher maternal body temperature during delivery
prolonged premature rupture of membranes (>18 hours)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 64 neonates diagnosed with Group B Streptococcus infection, identified from 16,022 neonates admitted to a nursery in Al-Madinah Al-Munawarah between 2017 and 2022.
finding: Neonatal GBS infection is prevalent in Al-Madinah Al-Munawarah, with associated risk factors including preterm labor, higher maternal body temperature during delivery, prolonged premature rupture of membranes, GBS bacteriuria, and unexamined mothers.
